name: How much does a detached ADU really cost in Los Angeles after utility upgrades?

mainEntity.name: How much does a detached ADU cost in Los Angeles once utility trenching, sewer connection, and panel upgrades are included?
mainEntity.text: How much does a detached ADU cost in Los Angeles once utility trenching, sewer connection, and panel upgrades are included?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest cost surprise in detached ADU projects is usually not the structure itself, but site and utility work. A quoted build price may cover framing, finishes, and standard construction, yet still exclude trenching, sewer lateral work, electrical panel upgrades, water service changes, and coordination with local utility providers. On many Los Angeles-area lots, those items can add a substantial amount to the total budget, especially when the main house is older or the ADU is placed far from existing service lines. Homeowners should ask for a fully itemized budget that separates hard construction costs from soft costs and utility allowances. The most useful bid is one that states what is included, what is provisional, and what triggers a change order. For accurate planning, compare at least two scopes: a base build estimate and a fully loaded estimate that includes site work, permits, and utility upgrades. This is the best way to avoid underbudgeting a detached ADU in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detached ADU in Los Angeles often costs far more than the base build price once utility work is added. Homeowners should budget separately for trenching, sewer tie-ins, electrical upgrades, water service changes, and LADWP-related fees, because those items can materially change the total project cost.
